title: Second-order arithmetic: full induction and categoricity
summary: Use induction over every subset to characterize the natural numbers, then see why full second-order compactness and larger-model conclusions fail.
abstract: The first-order Peano axioms allow elements beyond every ordinary natural-number numeral. Asking induction to apply to every subset changes the answer. One second-order sentence expresses that stronger requirement. Together with the usual arithmetic equations it forces every element to be reached from zero by finitely many successors, and determines addition and multiplication there. We prove that every full model of these finite axioms is isomorphic to the standard natural-number structure. The same argument explains a limitation of full second-order logic: a fresh constant can avoid any finite list of numerals, but no full Peano model lets it avoid them all. Compactness fails, and these finite axioms have an infinite full model but no uncountable one.
